### Project 5: [Orchestral Manoeuvres ~~in the Dark~~](https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=orchestral+manoeuvres+in+the+dark) over Wi-Fi

**Task:** 

1. Create an experience to enable **multiple users to
simultaneously use hand-phone gestures to create collaborative
music/sound**. 
1. Viewers must use dance and/or gestures holding
handphones, to create music together . 
1. **Each user must be able to
control unique aspects of the music** to create a collaborative piece
each time. 
1. There must be clear opportunities and instructions for
collaboration based on a **Stag Hunt / Coordination Game**. 

**Tools:**
`Software: Pure Data for sound synthesis; Android apps like Sensors2OSC for sensor data logging and sharing over WiFi`
`Hardware: WiFi network hotspot; Smartphones; Laptop or Raspberry Pi running PureData`\

**Ideas from our Course:**
`Proximity; Game Theory / Stag Hunt; Networks and Graphs`\

**Resources:**

-   <u>[PureData Sound Synthesizer](puredata.info)</u>\
-   <u>[Sensors2OSC](https://sensors2.org/osc/)</u>\

### Project 7: <u>Nightmare at Room 307</u>

**Task:** 

1. Create strange bloodcurdling sounds based on where individuals
are standing in the room. 
1. Participants need to move, perhaps be blindfolded and wear headphones / earphones.
1. If they can experience "pain" in some way based on location, that would also be good. `r emoji::emoji("rofl")`. 

**Tools:**
`Software: Geogebra or R/RStudio; Android apps for sensor data logging and sharing over WiFi`
`Hardware: WiFi network hotspot; Smartphones; Arduino with Wifi; Makey-Makey for position location based on footfall`

**Ideas from our Course:** `Proximity; Schelling Points`

**Resources:**

- [Theremin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theremin)

### Project 8: Friends (Season 65, Episode 12)

**Task:** 

1. Use this article in the Atlantic Magazine as inspiration: [How
friendships in Change in 
Adulthood](https://www.theatlantic.com/health/archive/2015/10/how-friendships-change-over-time-in-adulthood/411466/).
1. Create a physical graph/network related installation, based on personal, or crowd-sourced, or fictitious but plausible friendship data, and show in an interactive way how these friendship networks change over time.
1. Use our collected college network data, and inspiration from
<https://graphcommons.com> as a starting point. 
1. Can embed electronic
(lights) or computed elements ( touch ) , if desired from an aesthetic
point of view or to create/enhance Viewer participation. 
1. The installation should show small changes over “time” and must be
**wilfully and meaningfully degradable by viewers**. 
1. Water, ink, knives, or flame, rubber-bands and oil are possibilities. 1. No acid.

**Tools:**
`Software: None specified. graphcommons.com and RStudio are possibilities. Arduino can also be used for embedding computational elements.`
`Hardware: None specified. NO THERMOCOL.`

**Ideas from our Course:**
`Networks and Graphs; Connectors and Hubs; Network Dynamics and Measures; Erdos-Renyi / Watts-Strogatz / Barabasi-Albert models; Power Laws`

### Project 10: Way-Spotting Game

Now that we have an idea of `nodes`, `links` and `costs`, let us get an
experience of some more network science ideas:

1.  Head over to <https://medium.com/\\\@ran_katzir/teaching-network-science-using-board-games-f78489a3b3bd>
1. Make sense of the Board Game described there in detail. 
1. Build the Game!!
1.  Note if you can see the following:
    -   Frequently Used Nodes
    -   Frequently used Links

**Ideas from our Course:** `Network Traversal, Node Degree, Centrality, Betweenness, Link Values or Costs`
